thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: routing-service 'route-mixer' anomaly: sustained skew of traffic away from premium tier into low-cost lanes for the last 6m. Error spike on downstream inference nodes observed. Auto-alarms triggered.
alyssa: I'm oncall, looking now. First job: confirm customer impact and whether this is policy or infra.
samir: I can pull logs and policy diffs. seeing a batch of policy evaluations failing with 'fallback_to_default=true' more than usual. Possibly a policy evaluation timeout.
jordan: Product note: if premium traffic is getting cut, customers with SLAs could be affected. We need to assess few large tenants first.
nicole: Support reports 3 customer tickets referencing higher latency and occasional 5xxs in EU and US-west. Not high volume yet but prominent accounts.
alyssa: Ok, quick triage: 1) Are routing policy agents healthy? 2) Any recent deploys to smart-routing config? 3) Is quota enforcement misapplied? samir, can you run the policy-validator diff?
samir: Running validator now. Saw a config push from automated optimizer at 1859872000 that adjusted tier weights for cost-savings. Validator shows one rule using region-prefix matching that is miscompiled for long hostnames. Might be causing exceptions and triggering fallback. Patch suggestion ready.
ops-lead: @alyssa if fallback path is diverting traffic to low-cost lane we should throttle that lane asap to protect capacity. Can we apply temporary cap to free/low tier?
alyssa: Yes. Mitigation plan in this order: 1) Apply emergency cap to low-cost tier (rps cap + weight reduction). 2) Pause the optimizer autopilot pushing routing changes. 3) Hotpatch policy compilation bug. 4) Notify affected customers and update status page.
jordan: Agreed. I'll own customer comms once we have impact numbers. Nicole, collect ticket IDs and affected orgs.
nicole: Collected: ORG-3421, ORG-3427, ORG-3430. Two are premium customers; both reported 5xx + increased latency.
samir: Preparing API call to apply override now. Pasting command: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/routing/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "selector": {"tier": "low"},
    "override": {
      "weight": 0.1,
      "rate_limit": {"rps": 15},
      "ttl": 3600,
      "reason": "emergency mitigate fallback-induced skew"
    }
  }'
```
deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-override/1859876543 -> canary on route-mixer-hosts (3 nodes)
alyssa: Applying override now. Will monitor p50/p95 for premium tier and error rates. Samir, pause optimizer autopilot.
samir: Pausing autopilot: ```
POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/autopilot/pause
{ "component": "routing-optimizer", "duration": 7200 }
```
ops-lead: Throttle applied, seeing initial rate-limit in metrics. Premium p95 dropping toward baseline. Error count decreased by ~30% in the last 2m. Good sign.
jordan: Quick impact estimate: Before fix, ~7% of requests from premium tenants were hitting low-tier; current estimate affects ~1.8% of total traffic after throttle. We'll note that in comms.
nicole: Notifying customers: drafting status update — will flag SLAs and next steps.
alyssa: Samir — can you push hotpatch for the policy compiler? Keep patch minimal: guard against empty host fragments and fallback to explicit match. Test on staging then prod canary.
samir: Working on branch. Patch: ```diff
- parseHostPrefix(prefix) -> may throw
+ parseHostPrefix(prefix) { if (!prefix) return null; ... }
```
samir: Deploying patch to canary. deploy-bot: canary deploy initiated: route-compiler-hotfix/1859876543 -> 2 canary hosts
ops-lead: Observability: added temporary alert to page if fallback > 2% for premium tier while we finish.
jordan: Customer comms ready: short note, impact, mitigation done (temporary throttle), ETA for full fix 2h, will escalate if more customers hit.
nicole: Sent messages to ORG-3421 and ORG-3427. Both acknowledged and will monitor.
alyssa: Monitoring windows: 15m for stabilization, then consider rolling hotpatch to remaining hosts. If stable, remove override after compiler patch is rolled and autopilot remains paused.
samir: Canary looks good - compiler no longer throws on malformed prefix. Running a quick synthetic against route-mixer.
samir: Synthetic results: success rate back to normal, policy evaluation latency reduced from ~220ms to ~35ms.
ops-lead: Metrics steady. Error spike fully mitigated, premium p95 at baseline. Recommend staged rollout to non-canary.
alyssa: Rolling to 25% next. deploy-bot: rolling update -> route-compiler-hotfix -> 25% hosts
jordan: Preparing status page entry and internal postmortem stub. We'll capture root cause: optimizer produced a rule that wasn't validated for edge hostnames; compiler lacked defensive code. Also include playbook step to block autopilot changes to routing without canary validation.
nicole: No further customer escalations. Monitoring ongoing.
alyssa: Oncall handoff: I need to sign off at 19:00 UTC. samir, can you take the remainder of the window? I'll DM handoff checklist.
samir: I'll take it. If regression appears, page me and escalate to ops-lead.
alyssa: TL;DR Mitigations applied: emergency low-tier cap (rps/weight), autopilot paused, compiler hotfix canaried and rolling. Customer impact limited to small set; ongoing monitoring.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated. Next: postmortem required. Assigning to eng-runtime and devex for follow-up.
